audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 0-3 disagreed across layers: phases[].side read Lissandra on all seven rows while content win[] and packet.levelChart read Skill through level 5.
audit.why: Pre-6 Ekko pokes from 1075 with Timewinder's out-and-back hit while Lissandra's Q is 725; her advantage only arrives when Frozen Tomb answers Phase Dive. Levels 1-5 are genuinely even.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-3 moved to Skill as one atomic group, with the two whys that claimed a Lissandra advantage rewritten.

audit.whatIsWrong: Chronobreak's cooldown was never stated, and it is the one number that shapes the whole matchup: 110s at rank 1 but 50s at rank 3.
audit.why: A 110s window is an objective's worth of time without his escape; a 50s one is not. Advice to 'commit on its cooldown' means nothing without the number.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns and ahead now carry the 110/50 split so the player knows how large the punish window actually is.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2].text credited Ekko with a 'passive shield'. Z-Drive Resonance grants bonus damage and a burst of speed — the shield comes from Parallel Convergence (W), and only when he walks into his own anomaly. Nothing on the page mentioned that Phase Dive opens with an auto-attack reset, or that Chronobreak both goes untargetable and heals off damage received.
audit.why: missingInteractions flags all three: untargetable-dodges-burst, needs-antiheal and autoreset-burst-tell. The shield error tells a player to burst through something that is not there.
audit.corrected: Shield attributed to Parallel Convergence with its 22s cooldown and walk-in condition; the E auto-reset named as the wind-up cue; anti-heal added where extended trades are planned.

audit.why: It is the field that carries real cooldowns.
audit.corrected: Chronobreak 110s to 50s, Parallel Convergence 22s, Frozen Tomb 120s stated.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was tradeGood verbatim and dontsFull[2].d was tradeBad verbatim under unrelated titles; dosFull[0].d and dosFull[2].d also carried bodies that did not answer their titles.
audit.corrected: Four bullet bodies rewritten to their own titles using Phase Dive's 325 range and 9s cooldown, the claw's 1050/24s, and Chronobreak's rewind-and-heal.

edits.before: Q-shatter the wave and chip his melee step-ups — your early Q harass is better than the lane gives it credit for.
edits.after: Level 1 is even: he pokes Timewinder from 1075 and you Q-shatter at 725 — neither of you can convert it yet.

edits.before: Lost Chapter timing — Q spam stops hurting your mana. Chip Ekko every time he touches the wave.
edits.after: Even: his W anomaly needs 22s and a walk-in to stun, and your root answers Phase Dive on 8s.

edits.before: - Ekko Chronobreak: matchup-defining — Erases your kill and bursts back — track the hologram and save final damage for after it. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your R Frozen Tomb (self-cast) like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Chronobreak is 110s at rank 1 but only 50s at rank 3 — he goes untargetable and heals, so hold your last spell until the rewind is spent. - Parallel Convergence is 22s and only stuns if he walks into it. - Frozen Tomb is 120s: kill windows only.

edits.before: Ekko wins by landing Chronobreak, denying your pattern, and front-loading the violence while your kit is still stretching.
edits.after: Ekko wins by chipping with Timewinder's return, stunning you in Parallel Convergence, then erasing your counter-kill with Chronobreak.

edits.before: Ahead, hunt: claw into every river skirmish first, tomb the carry, and snowball picks — Ekko farming under tower can't stop a roaming Lissandra.
edits.after: Ahead, deny the reset: Chronobreak is 110s at rank 1, so force it early and take every objective in the two minutes he plays without it.

edits.before: Carry through picks — claw-root-tomb converts vision into kills better than any control mage; the map shrinks every time your E is up.
edits.after: Carry by ignoring the flicker — a point-and-click tomb catches Ekko wherever Phase Dive puts him, and Chronobreak cannot rewind a stun.

edits.before: If Ekko takes first blood, tighten up: Chronobreak is now always up in your head. A second kill means the duel is over and the game isn’t — farm with Q shatters and stay relevant through self-R utility.
edits.after: If Ekko takes first blood, tighten up: Chronobreak is now always up in your head. A second kill ends the duel — buy Grievous Wounds so the rewind heal shrinks, farm Q shatters, stay relevant through self-R utility.

edits.before: Erases your kill and bursts back — track the hologram and save final damage for after it. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: Phase Dive is 325 range on 9s at rank 1 and opens with an auto reset — the wind-up is the cue, not the cast. Stand where W answers it.

edits.before: Q-shatter his wave contact, and when he steps to punish, W-root into full rotation and walk — the root tax makes every aggressive step expensive.
edits.after: Dark ice makes you untargetable and invulnerable — his Z-Drive combo lands on nothing, and you come out to root a 7s Phase Dive.

edits.before: Ekko whiffs Chronobreak and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: Your claw is 1050 range on 24s — leave before his W lands.

edits.before: The claw is your entrance AND your exit — spending both directions on one greedy play is how Lissandras die famous.
edits.after: A 120s Frozen Tomb spent on Timewinder chip leaves nothing for the Chronobreak fight that decides the lane.

edits.before: Clawing in with W on cooldown 'to poke' — an engage tool spent on chip damage is a Lissandra standing in melee range with no ice left.
edits.after: Chronobreak rewinds him to where he stood seconds ago and heals him off your damage — chasing it just walks you into his jungler.

edits.before: With Everfrost or Liandry's you E-in, W-root and R him faster than his passive shield or W stun can save him.
edits.after: With Everfrost or Liandry's you E-in, W-root and R him faster than his Parallel Convergence shield or stun can save him.

notes: Content win[0..6] already matched packet.levelChart, so only the stale full-layer sides moved; no win[N] twin edits existed to make. Ratings left alone. Not asserted: whether Frozen Tomb's stun applied to Ekko before he casts Chronobreak prevents the rewind (his R is not listed as cleansing CC, but Riot's text does not say either way), whether Parallel Convergence's stun is reduced by tenacity, and whether Lissandra's self-R invulnerability nullifies the Chronobreak arrival damage.
